mainTopic: Comparing the case of a ספר תורה to the hide of the קרבן פסח on שבת, and defining an open versus closed מבוי for rescuing items from a fire
overview: The amud opens in the middle of an argument. The חכמים compared saving a ספר תורה in its case to handling the hide of the קרבן פסח on שבת. The גמרא rejects two versions of this comparison. A third version is proposed: one may bring a case with money in it to rescue the scroll. The גמרא then finds no source for that rule. מר בר רב אשי returns to the original comparison and says the case is one where the person does not want the hide. When challenged with פסיק רישיה, he answers that the hide is removed in strips. The גמרא then turns to the משנה's open and closed מבוי. רב חסדא defines them as three walls with one or two posts, following רבי אליעזר. רבה rejects this and defines them as two walls with one or two posts, following רבי יהודה. אביי then turns רבה's own objection about food and drink back on him, and the discussion continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The case and the hide are not comparable
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects comparing the ספר תורה case to the hide of the פסח. The case holds something permitted, but the hide holds something forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: Are they really the same? There, the case is a base for something permitted. Here, the hide is a base for something forbidden!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the comparison the חכמים made between saving a ספר תורה with its case and moving the hide of the פסח together with its meat.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A case holding a ספר תורה serves something you may move on שבת. The hide is attached to meat of the פסח, which may not be moved yet. So the hide is a בסיס לדבר האסור, and the comparison seems to fall apart.

keyTerms.meaning: Are they comparable? (a formula that rejects a comparison)
A base: an object that holds something else
Something permitted to move on שבת
Something forbidden to move on שבת (מוקצה)

steps.confusionAlert: This amud starts in the middle of an argument. Before it, the חכמים argued: if we may save a ספר תורה's case along with the scroll, we should also be able to handle the hide of the פסח along with the meat.

phrases.english: Are they comparable?!
There, it became a base for a permitted object,
phrases.notes: The case holds the ספר תורה.

phrases.english: Here, it became a base for a forbidden object!
phrases.notes: The hide holds the meat of the פסח.

steps.kashyaTarget: The comparison between the ספר תורה case and the hide of the פסח
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The case serves something permitted, while the hide serves something forbidden, so the two cases are different.

steps.title: Second version: a case that also has money inside
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rewords the argument. Even a case with forbidden coins inside may be saved, so the hide should be movable too.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, this is what they said to him: if we may save a ספר תורה's case along with the scroll, even though there is money inside it, shouldn't we be able to move the hide along with the meat?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא fixes the comparison by rewording what the חכמים actually meant.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now the case is also holding coins, which are מוקצה. Even so, the משנה lets you save it. So the fact that the hide holds something forbidden should not matter either.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather, this is what they said to him (a rewording of the argument)
Case, casing
Coins, money (מוקצה on שבת)
Together with, by way of

phrases.english: Rather, this is what they said to him:

phrases.aramaic: אִם מַצִּילִין תִּיק שֶׁל סֵפֶר עִם הַסֵּפֶר,
phrases.english: If one may rescue the case of a scroll along with the scroll,

phrases.aramaic: וְאַף עַל פִּי שֶׁיֵּשׁ בְּתוֹכוֹ מָעוֹת,
phrases.english: even though there is money inside it,
shall we not move the hide together with the meat?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 1 by rewording the comparison.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The comparison was about a case holding only the ספר תורה.
steps.terutzMaskana: The comparison is about a case that holds both the scroll and money.

steps.title: Still not comparable: partly permitted versus fully forbidden
steps.stepSummary: The case holds both a permitted and a forbidden item. The hide holds only a forbidden item.
steps.simpleTranslation: Are they comparable? There, the case is a base for both something forbidden and something permitted. Here, it is entirely a base for something forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the second version of the comparison as well.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When a בסיס holds both permitted and forbidden items, the permitted one can make it movable. The ספר תורה makes the case movable. The hide holds nothing permitted at all, so the gap remains.

keyTerms.meaning: Entirely, all of it
A base for both a forbidden and a permitted item

phrases.english: Are they comparable?

phrases.aramaic: הָתָם נַעֲשָׂה בָּסִיס לְדָבָר הָאָסוּר וּלְדָבָר הַמּוּתָּר,
phrases.english: There, it became a base for a forbidden object and a permitted object,

phrases.aramaic: הָכָא — כּוּלּוֹ נַעֲשָׂה בָּסִיס לְדָבָר הָאָסוּר.
phrases.english: here, it is entirely a base for a forbidden object.

steps.kashyaTarget: The second version of the comparison
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A mixed base can be moved because of its permitted contents. A base for only forbidden items cannot.

steps.title: Third version: bringing a case full of money to save the scroll
steps.stepSummary: A case that holds only money may be brought from elsewhere to save a ספר תורה. That makes it like the hide.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, this is what they said to him: if one may bring a case with money inside from somewhere else in order to save a ספר תורה in it, shouldn't we be able to move the hide along with the meat?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rewords the comparison a third time to match the hide case exactly.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the case starts out holding only money, so at that moment it is entirely a base for something forbidden. Even so, you may bring it to rescue the scroll. That parallels the hide, which holds only forbidden meat.

keyTerms.meaning: One may bring
From elsewhere, from outside
To rescue

phrases.english: Rather, this is what they said to him:

phrases.aramaic: אִם מְבִיאִין תִּיק שֶׁיֵּשׁ בְּתוֹכוֹ מָעוֹת מֵעָלְמָא
phrases.english: If one may bring a case that has money inside it from elsewhere
to rescue a Torah scroll in it,
shall we not move the hide together with the meat?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 3 with a version that matches the hide exactly.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The case already held the scroll when it was moved.
steps.terutzMaskana: The case held only money when it was picked up, just like the hide.

steps.title: Where do we learn this rule itself?
steps.stepSummary: The rule about bringing a money-filled case from elsewhere is not in the משנה. So what is its source?
steps.simpleTranslation: And this rule itself, where do we know it from?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now questions the new premise it just used. This sets up the next attempts to find a source.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה only allows saving a case that already holds the scroll. The third version depends on a rule the משנה never states. So the גמרא needs a source for it.

keyTerms.meaning: And this itself
From where do we know it?

phrases.english: And this itself, from where do we know it?

steps.sheelahInformationSought: The source that permits bringing a money-filled case to rescue a ספר תורה.

steps.title: Proposed source: we need not dump the money, so we may also bring it
steps.stepSummary: The proposed source: since we need not empty the coins from a case that holds the scroll, we may also bring a case that holds coins.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you say: since when the case has money in it we do not throw the money out, we may also bring a case with money in it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא suggests a logical source by stretching the משנה's rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה lets you carry the case without first dumping the coins. The suggestion is that this also allows bringing a coin-filled case from somewhere else.

keyTerms.meaning: If you say (introduces a suggestion that will be rejected)
Throws
To bring

phrases.english: If you say: since in a case where there is money in it
one does not throw it out,
we may also bring it —

steps.raayaObject: Permission to bring a coin-filled case
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה's rule that one need not dump the coins before saving the case

steps.title: Rejected: emptying costs time in a fire, but the money could be dumped first
steps.stepSummary: In the משנה, stopping to empty the coins could let the fire burn the scroll. When bringing a case, he could just dump the coins first.
steps.simpleTranslation: Are they comparable? There, while he is busy emptying it, the fire may catch the scroll. Here, while he is doing this, let him throw the money out.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the proposed source.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה's leniency exists only because of urgency: emptying the case wastes time while the scroll burns. When fetching a case from elsewhere, there is time to dump the coins, so the leniency does not carry over.

keyTerms.meaning: In the meantime
Fire
Let him throw them out

phrases.english: Are they comparable?!
There, in the meantime the fire may catch,
here, in the meantime let him throw them out.

steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the proposed source for the third version of the comparison.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The משנה's leniency is based on the urgency of the fire, which does not apply when bringing a case from elsewhere.

steps.title: מר בר רב אשי returns to the original comparison
steps.stepSummary: מר בר רב אשי drops the rewordings and keeps the original simple comparison.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, מר בר רב אשי said: really, it is as we said at first.
steps.whatsHappening: Since the third version has no source, מר בר רב אשי goes back to the very first comparison. This prepares for his answer to the objection against it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The original comparison simply linked the ספר תורה case to the hide of the פסח. He keeps it, but he still has to answer the earlier objection that flaying is a full מלאכה.

keyTerms.meaning: An אמורא, son of רב אשי
Really, actually (returns to an earlier position)
At first, originally

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא אָמַר מָר בַּר רַב אָשֵׁי:
phrases.english: Rather, Mar bar Rav Ashi said:
Actually, it is as we said at first.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא אָמַר מָר בַּר רַב אָשֵׁי לְעוֹלָם כִּדְאָמְרִינַן מֵעִיקָּרָא
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The original comparison stands, and the rewordings are unnecessary.

steps.title: Flaying is not a מלאכה when he does not want the hide
steps.stepSummary: Moving the case is only טלטול, while flaying is a מלאכה. The answer: the case is one where he does not need the hide.
steps.simpleTranslation: And as for what bothered you, that here it is only moving and there it is a forbidden labor: it is a case where he does not want the hide.
steps.whatsHappening: מר בר רב אשי answers an earlier objection: moving the case is just טלטול, but flaying is a real מלאכה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If he does not want the hide, the flaying is not done for its own purpose. According to רבי שמעון, that makes him exempt, so flaying becomes comparable to mere טלטול.

keyTerms.meaning: Moving an object (a rabbinic issue on שבת)
A forbidden labor (a Torah prohibition)
For example, it is a case where
Hide, skin

phrases.english: And as for what was difficult for you:
here it is moving, and here it is a forbidden labor —
it is a case where he does not need the hide.

steps.terutzHavaAmina: Flaying is always a full מלאכה.
steps.terutzMaskana: When he does not need the hide, flaying is not a punishable מלאכה (following רבי שמעון).

steps.title: Challenge from פסיק רישיה ולא ימות
steps.stepSummary: אביי and רבא say that רבי שמעון agrees a person is liable when the result is unavoidable. Flaying unavoidably produces a hide.
steps.simpleTranslation: But אביי and רבא both said: רבי שמעון agrees in a case of 'cut off its head and will it not die?'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges מר בר רב אשי's answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Not wanting the result helps only when the result is uncertain. When a result is certain (פסיק רישיה), even רבי שמעון holds the person liable. Flaying certainly produces a hide, so not wanting it should not help.

keyTerms.meaning: Two major אמוראים
Agrees, concedes
Cut off its head and will it not die? An action whose result is unavoidable
A תנא who exempts a דבר שאין מתכוין (an unintended result)

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think רבי שמעון always exempts unintended results. If the result is guaranteed, he agrees the person is liable.
steps.whyThisMatters: פסיק רישיה is a basic rule of הלכות שבת that comes up across ש״ס and in practical הלכה.

phrases.english: But Abaye and Rava both said:
Rabbi Shimon concedes
in a case of 'cut off its head and will it not die' —

steps.kashyaTarget: מר בר רב אשי's case of not needing the hide
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Flaying unavoidably produces a hide, so it is a פסיק רישיה, and even רבי שמעון would hold him liable.

steps.title: He flays it in strips
steps.stepSummary: He removes the hide in small strips, so no usable hide is produced.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is a case where he takes it off in strips.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the פסיק רישיה challenge.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the hide comes off in strips, no usable hide is created. So there is no unavoidable forbidden result, and רבי שמעון's exemption still works.

keyTerms.meaning: Takes, removes
In strips

steps.whatToRemember: The comparison to the ספר תורה case holds. Flaying the פסח is only like טלטול when he does not want the hide and removes it in strips.

phrases.english: It is where he removes it strip by strip.

steps.terutzHavaAmina: Flaying always produces a usable hide.
steps.terutzMaskana: Strip-by-strip flaying produces no hide, so it is not a פסיק רישיה.

steps.title: What is an open versus a closed מבוי?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא goes back to the משנה, which allows rescuing items into a מבוי, and asks how open and closed alleys are defined.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'And to where may one rescue them?' etc. What is an open alley, and what is an alley that is not open?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic by quoting the משנה. It sets up a definition question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the משנה, the תנא קמא allows rescuing only into a closed מבוי, and בן בתירא allows even an open one. The גמרא needs to know exactly what each term means.

keyTerms.meaning: One may rescue
What is the case? How is it defined?
Open, passing through
Etcetera (the quote of the משנה continues)

phrases.english: 'And to where may one rescue them,' etc.
What are the circumstances of an open alley,
what are the circumstances of one that is not open?

steps.sheelahInformationSought: The definitions of an open and a closed מבוי in the משנה.

steps.title: רב חסדא: two posts means closed, one post means open
steps.stepSummary: Three walls with two posts is a closed מבוי. Three walls with one post is an open מבוי.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חסדא said: three walls and two posts is an alley that is not open. Three walls and one post is an open alley.
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא defines the two kinds of מבוי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here 'open' does not mean having no walls. It means an alley that lacks the full fix of two posts at its entrance. A single לחי leaves it counted as open.

keyTerms.meaning: An אמורא
Walls, partitions
Posts placed at the entrance of an alley
An alley that opens onto a public domain

steps.confusionAlert: Both kinds have three walls. The only difference is one post versus two at the entrance.

phrases.english: Rav Chisda said:
three walls and two posts —
this is an alley that is not open.
Three walls and one post —
this is an open alley.

steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Two posts make a closed מבוי. One post makes an open מבוי.

steps.title: Both opinions follow רבי אליעזר's view on fixing a מבוי
steps.stepSummary: The תנא קמא and בן בתירא both follow רבי אליעזר, who requires two posts. Source: the dispute about הכשר מבוי.
steps.simpleTranslation: Both of them follow רבי אליעזר, as we learned: to fix an alley, בית שמאי say a post and a beam, בית הלל say either a post or a beam, and רבי אליעזר says two posts.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why two posts are the standard. It shows that both opinions in the משנה are built on רבי אליעזר's view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Only רבי אליעזר requires two posts to make a מבוי fully usable. So a מבוי with one post is not yet fixed by his standard, which is why it is called 'open'. Under בית הלל, one post would already be enough.

keyTerms.meaning: According to the view of
Making an alley fit for carrying on שבת
A beam across the entrance
A תנא who requires two posts
The two classic schools of the תנאים

steps.whatToRemember: Open versus closed depends on the number of posts, according to רבי אליעזר's requirement of two לחיים for הכשר מבוי.

phrases.english: And both of them follow the view of Rabbi Eliezer,
as we learned in a Mishnah: preparing an alley —
Beit Shammai say: a post and a beam,

phrases.aramaic: וּבֵית הִלֵּל אוֹמְרִים: אוֹ לֶחִי אוֹ קוֹרָה.
phrases.english: and Beit Hillel say: either a post or a beam.
Rabbi Eliezer says: two posts.

steps.raayaObject: רב חסדא's definition using two posts versus one
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה in עירובין about הכשר מבוי, where רבי אליעזר requires two posts

steps.title: רבה objects: three walls is not an 'open' alley
steps.stepSummary: רבה argues that a מבוי with three walls and only one post cannot be called 'open'.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה said to him: An alley with three walls and one post, you call that 'open'?
steps.whatsHappening: רבה challenges רב חסדא's definition from Step 13. He says the name 'open' does not fit an alley that has three walls.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An alley with three walls is physically closed on three sides. It is only missing a second post, which is a technical requirement according to רבי אליעזר. Lacking a technical fix makes the alley not yet usable, but it does not make it 'open' (מפולש). So רב חסדא's label does not match reality.

keyTerms.meaning: Open-through: an alley open at both ends, like a passageway
Three walls
A post set at the alley's entrance as a symbolic marker
You call it

phrases.english: Rabba said to him (to Rav Chisda):
three walls and one post
you call that 'open'?!
phrases.notes: Rhetorical. It is plainly a closed alley.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַבָּה: שָׁלֹשׁ מְחִיצּוֹת וְלֶחִי אֶחָד ״מְפוּלָּשׁ״ קָרֵית לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the definition given in Step 13 and its grounding in Step 14.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב חסדא's definition of an open מבוי as three walls plus one post.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The word מפולש means open-through. A three-walled alley is physically closed and is only missing a technical post, so the term does not fit.

steps.title: רבה's second objection: then food and drink could be rescued too
steps.stepSummary: For the רבנן of the משנה, the closed alley (three walls, two posts) would be fully permitted, so the משנה should allow rescuing food and drink there, not only sacred writings.
steps.simpleTranslation: And furthermore: according to the רבנן, let us rescue food and drink into it!
steps.whatsHappening: רבה adds a second, stronger objection to רב חסדא's definition.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The רבנן here are the תנא קמא of the משנה, who allow rescue into a 'not open' alley. Under רב חסדא, that alley has three walls and two posts, so carrying there is fully permitted even by רבי אליעזר's standard. Under רב חסדא's reading, the משנה's closed alley would therefore be a fully permitted place according to the רבנן. If so, the rescue should not be limited to holy writings. Food and drink should be allowed there too.

keyTerms.meaning: And furthermore: introduces an additional objection
The Sages (the majority view)
Let us rescue into it
Food and drink

steps.confusionAlert: The question is not about saving food from a fire in general. It is this: if the place is already permitted for carrying, why does the משנה speak only of sacred writings?

phrases.english: And furthermore, according to the Rabbis,
let us rescue food and drink into it!
phrases.notes: The רבנן of the משנה allow rescue into the closed alley, which under רב חסדא is fully permitted, so carrying anything there should be allowed.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְעוֹד, לְרַבָּנַן נַצִּיל לְתוֹכוֹ אוֹכָלִין וּמַשְׁקִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second objection to the one in Step 15.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב חסדא's definition as applied to the view of the רבנן.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Under רב חסדא's definition, the closed alley is fully permitted according to the רבנן. That would make the משנה's restriction to sacred writings meaningless.

steps.title: רבה's own definition: two walls with two posts or one post
steps.stepSummary: רבה redefines the terms. Two walls with two posts is a closed מבוי, and two walls with one post is an open מבוי.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רבה said: two walls and two posts is an alley that is not open. Two walls and one post is an open alley.
steps.whatsHappening: רבה rejects רב חסדא's definition. He gives a new answer to the original question from Step 12: what are open and closed alleys?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Two walls means a passage open at both ends, like a street. With a post at each end it counts as 'not open'. With a post at only one end it counts as 'open'. This shifts the whole discussion from three-walled alleys to two-walled passages.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather: rejects the earlier view and introduces a new one
Two walls (a passage open at both ends)
Two posts, one at each end
An alley that is not open (closed)

phrases.english: Rather, Rabba said:
two walls and two posts —
that is an alley that is not open.
two walls and one post —
that is an open alley.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא אָמַר רַבָּה: שְׁתֵּי מְחִיצּוֹת וּשְׁנֵי לְחָיַיִן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces רב חסדא's definition, which Steps 15 and 16 rejected.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: How are the closed and open alleys of the משנה defined?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Two walls with two posts is closed. Two walls with one post is open.

steps.title: Both opinions in the משנה follow רבי יהודה
steps.stepSummary: רבה grounds his definition in a ברייתא. רבי יהודה allows a two-walled public area to be enclosed with a post or beam at each end. The רבנן disagree.
steps.simpleTranslation: Both the תנא קמא and בן בתירא follow רבי יהודה. As a ברייתא teaches: Furthermore, רבי יהודה said: One who has two houses on two sides of the public domain may put a post here and a post there, or a beam here and a beam there, and carry in between. They said to him: One may not make an עירוב for the public domain this way.
steps.whatsHappening: רבה shows the source for his reading. Both opinions in the משנה follow רבי יהודה's lenient view on two-walled areas.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה holds that two walls with a symbolic post or beam at both ends make a permitted area. So the 'not open' alley of the משנה, with two posts, is acceptable to him. The 'open' alley, with one post, is the one only בן בתירא allows. The רבנן of the ברייתא reject this setup, especially in a public domain.

keyTerms.meaning: Both of them (the two opinions in the משנה)
In accordance with רבי יהודה
A beam laid across the entrance as a symbolic marker
Carries and places, meaning carrying is allowed
One may not make an עירוב (combine into a permitted domain)

steps.whyThisMatters: This ties רבה's definition to an existing view in the dispute over הכשר מבוי, just as רב חסדא tied his own to רבי אליעזר in Step 14.

phrases.english: And both of them follow Rabbi Yehuda.

phrases.aramaic: דְּתַנְיָא, יָתֵר עַל כֵּן אָמַר רַבִּי יְהוּדָה:
phrases.english: As it was taught: Furthermore, Rabbi Yehuda said:
one who has two houses
on two sides of the public domain —
he makes a post here and a post there,
or a beam here and a beam there,
and he may carry and place things in between.
They (the Rabbis) said to him:
One may not make an eiruv for the public domain this way.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies the source behind רבה's definition in Step 17.
steps.raayaObject: רבה's definition of closed and open alleys as two-walled passages.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא in which רבי יהודה permits a two-walled area enclosed by a post or beam at each end.

steps.title: אביי: the food-and-drink problem hits your view too
steps.stepSummary: אביי turns רבה's second objection back on him. Under רבה's definition the closed alley is also permitted, so food and drink should be rescuable there.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to him: According to you as well, according to the רבנן, let us rescue food and drink into it!
steps.whatsHappening: אביי answers רבה by showing that רבה's own definition faces the same problem רבה raised in Step 16.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Under רבה's definition, the closed alley (two walls, two posts) is a permitted place according to the view that the רבנן of the משנה follow. If carrying is permitted there anyway, the משנה should not limit the rescue to sacred writings. So the 'furthermore' objection does not single out רב חסדא's view.

keyTerms.meaning: According to you as well: turns a challenge back on its author

steps.whatToRemember: Neither definition has yet escaped the question of why only sacred writings, and not food and drink, may be rescued into the closed alley. The sugya must still resolve this.

phrases.english: Abaye said to him (to Rabba):
according to you as well, according to the Rabbis,
let us rescue food and drink into it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Mirrors רבה's objection from Step 16 against רבה's own definition from Step 17.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבה's definition of the closed alley.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the closed alley is permitted according to the רבנן, the משנה's restriction to sacred writings makes no sense. This is the same flaw רבה found in רב חסדא's definition.
